investigations.question: When RestoreCommittedLogs replays committed entries inside NewRaft, can the replay fail to make progress because the FSM batch channel is produced into before its only consumer is started?
investigations.hypothesis: processLogs enqueues ceil(replayed/MaxAppendEntries) commitTuple batches into fsmMutateCh (capacity 128) during NewRaft, while runFSM, the only consumer of that channel, is started only after NewRaft returns; a replay of more than 128*MaxAppendEntries committed entries beyond the last snapshot should therefore block NewRaft permanently on the channel send, since shutdownCh can only be closed by Shutdown() on a *Raft that NewRaft never returns.
investigations.discriminator: Compare NewRaft return for replay sizes at and above the batch-capacity boundary, including a real cluster restart with and without a snapshot bounding the replay; a return in every case would refute the hypothesis.

investigations.question: When an explicit LeadershipTransferToServer names a member that is a non-voter, does the transfer admit the request, and what does the returned future and the voters' terms show when the target cannot win any election?
investigations.hypothesis: leaderLoop accepts any id present in leaderState.replState, which startStopReplication creates for non-voters as well, so nothing checks suffrage for an explicit target; leadershipTransfer then replicates the non-voter up to the last index and sends TimeoutNow, timeoutNow makes the non-voter a transfer-candidate, and electSelf raises its term and asks every voter, whose requestVote handler raises its own term and steps down before rejecting the non-voter. The caller's future can then complete without error while leadership moved to an unrequested voter, contradicting the documented graceful failure for a follower that cannot be promoted.
investigations.discriminator: A real cluster in which one member is demoted to non-voter, followed by an explicit transfer to that member: record the future's result, whether the named target ever becomes leader, the interval with no leader, and the voters' terms before and after. A future that reports an error, or a target that wins, would refute the hypothesis.

investigations.question: Can a heartbeat delivered through the concurrent fast-path lower the persisted current term after the main thread has observed a higher one, and can the node then truncate and apply an entry from a stale leader at an index it had already committed at the higher term?
investigations.hypothesis: The Transport contract permits SetHeartbeatHandler callbacks to run outside the main RPC queue, and NetworkTransport dispatches heartbeats from its connection handler, so processHeartbeat can execute appendEntries concurrently with the main thread. appendEntries tests a.Term > r.getCurrentTerm() and then calls setCurrentTerm(a.Term), which unconditionally persists and stores the term, so a heartbeat carrying an older term that read the current term before the main thread adopted a higher one can write its older term afterwards. If the term then regresses, the AppendEntries older-term rejection no longer blocks the stale leader, whose conflicting entry at an already committed index is truncated and applied.
investigations.discriminator: Since a fast-path heartbeat only writes the term, the leader and last contact, the decisive observation is whether a concurrent heartbeat's term write can land after the main thread has persisted a higher term for the same node. Deliver one heartbeat carrying an intermediate term through the registered handler on a separate goroutine while the main thread processes a higher-term AppendEntries, using a stable store that makes the two term writes concurrent, and record the persisted term sequence plus the node's log and applied state before and after. A persisted term that never decreases, or entries that are never replaced afterwards, would refute the hypothesis.

investigations.question: Can VerifyLeader report success while the leader can reach fewer voters than its voter quorum, because acknowledgements from non-voter replication streams are counted toward that quorum?
investigations.hypothesis: verifyLeader sizes the quorum with quorumSize, which counts voters only, but registers the verify future on every followerReplication in leaderState.replState, and startStopReplication creates one for every configured server including non-voters; a successful heartbeat from a non-voter calls notifyAll(true) and increments the verify future's vote count, so a leader that can reach only itself among voters can still reach the voter-sized quorum with non-voter acknowledgements and report success.
investigations.discriminator: Boot five members, demote two to non-voters, cut the leader from the two remaining voters but leave the non-voters reachable, and ask the leader to verify itself with a bounded wait; compare against the same cluster with the non-voters also cut. A success in the trigger and a failure in the control establishes that non-voter acknowledgements substitute for voter support.

investigations.question: When a leader's log write for a configuration change fails, is the new configuration still installed in memory, and can the node then elect itself and commit client entries with a quorum that the committed configuration does not recognise?
investigations.hypothesis: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry and then unconditionally calls setLatestConfiguration, commitment.setConfiguration and startStopReplication with the new configuration at the index the entry would have had, while dispatchLogs on a StoreLogs error only answers the futures and steps the node down. The in-memory latest configuration therefore describes a log entry that does not exist, and because quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState all read that latest configuration, a leader that failed to remove a voter can re-elect itself with the smaller quorum and commit alone.
investigations.discriminator: Two real voters with a store that fails exactly the configuration write: after the failed RemoveServer, compare the in-memory latest configuration index with the last stored log index, then let the node stand for election and apply a command, and compare the resulting commit index with the last log index on the other voter. A latest index inside the stored log, or a commit that the peer has, would refute the hypothesis.

knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; no snapshot restored at or above the staged commit index.

knowledge.statement: Automatic leadership transfer and explicit leadership transfer use different target checks: pickServer (used when no id is given) skips every server whose Suffrage is not Voter, while an explicit id is only looked up in leaderState.replState, which contains an entry for every configured server including non-voters, and a successful lookup proceeds to replicate and send TimeoutNow without consulting the target's suffrage.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state with a committed latest configuration containing a non-voter; explicit LeadershipTransferToServer(id) for that member.

knowledge.statement: The Transport interface documents SetHeartbeatHandler as a fast-path that avoids head-of-line blocking and tells transports that do not support it to push heartbeats onto the Consumer channel; NetworkTransport stores the callback and, for a request shaped like a heartbeat, calls it directly on the connection-handler goroutine, while InmemTransport ignores the call entirely. NewRaft registers r.processHeartbeat, which forwards the request to appendEntries.
knowledge.conditions: Transport implementing the heartbeat fast-path (NetworkTransport); NewRaft has completed and registered the handler.

knowledge.statement: NetworkTransport's connection handler decodes an AppendEntries request and treats it as a heartbeat exactly when the term is non-zero, a leader address is present, PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm are both zero, there are no entries and LeaderCommitIndex is zero; for that shape it looks up the registered heartbeat handler under its lock and, if set, calls it directly on the connection-handler goroutine and skips the consumer channel, otherwise it enqueues the request for the main thread.
knowledge.conditions: NetworkTransport with NewRaft having registered processHeartbeat; incoming AppendEntries request matching the heartbeat field pattern.

knowledge.statement: verifyLeader arms the verification with the leader's own vote by setting the future's vote count to one, sizes the quorum with quorumSize, which counts voters only, and then registers that future on every entry of leaderState.replState, which startStopReplication creates for every configured server including non-voters; a successful heartbeat or AppendEntries from any of those streams calls notifyAll(true), whose vote increments the count and completes the verification once it reaches the quorum. With three voters the quorum is two, so the leader plus one non-voter acknowledgement completes a verification that no second voter supported.
knowledge.conditions: Leader with at least one non-voter replication stream and fewer reachable voters than the voter quorum.

knowledge.statement: RecoverCluster refuses to run without existing state, restores the newest usable snapshot, then replays every log entry after the snapshot index, applying only LogCommand entries to the FSM and tracking the last index and term; it then writes a new snapshot carrying the caller-supplied configuration with configuration index 1 and deletes the entire log range. The recovered configuration is therefore the operator's parameter rather than anything derived from the log, and entries the node held without cluster-wide commitment become part of the recovered baseline.
knowledge.conditions: Operator-invoked catastrophic recovery with existing log, stable or snapshot state.

scope.description: Four restart attempts with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: a commit-tracking store seeded with 8192 committed command entries (exactly 128 batches), the same seeded store with 8193 entries (129 batches), and two restarts of the same-address retained state produced by a real single-node cluster that committed 8300 commands through the normal leader/commit/apply path, one after an explicit Snapshot() and one without a snapshot.
assumptions: The FSM batch channel capacity and MaxAppendEntries are constants of the captured code; the harness records both in every case event.
Each case builds its own stores and transport, so cases do not share state; the real-prefix cases reuse exactly the stores written by the producing raft.
NewRaft is invoked on its own goroutine and observed for a bounded window; a case that never returns is reported as returned=false rather than as a harness failure.
fsm_applied_sampled is a single observation at the end of the window, not a completion marker.
excluded: No assertions about commit safety, voting or membership; this probe addresses startup progress only.
Snapshots older than the staged commit index by fewer than 8193 entries are not varied; the with-snapshot control removes the replay entirely.

basis.prefix: Per case the harness creates an InmemCommitTrackingStore (and InmemSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, assuranceFSM) and emits startup_case_<case> with the staged commit index, last log index, snapshot index and derived replay batch count. Seeded cases store LogCommand entries 1..N and stage commit index N. Real-prefix cases call BootstrapCluster for a single voter, start the producing raft with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, wait for leadership, apply 8300 commands through Apply futures on the leader, optionally call Snapshot(), then Shutdown(). The restart then calls NewRaft with a fresh Config (RestoreCommittedLogs=true), a fresh FSM and a fresh transport on the retained stores, bounded by the case timeout; startup_result_<case> records returned, elapsed_ms, error, sampled FSM apply count and the number of newly blocked processLogs/restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutines relative to a pre-case stack sample.
basis.responsibility: The library, not the caller, owns the size and lifetime of its FSM dispatch channel: it chooses the batch size, creates fsmMutateCh, and decides the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs on disk before completing NewRaft, so it must complete for a legal (store, commit index) state rather than block the caller that cannot yet shut it down.

comparisons.description: Exactly 128 replay batches (the channel capacity) must still let NewRaft complete.
A real-prefix restart whose snapshot bounds the replay must let NewRaft complete.
One entry past the 128-batch capacity must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.
A real cluster restart with 130 replay batches must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.

semantic_changes: The startup case event now records the MaxAppendEntries actually configured for that case rather than the default constant; the four retained cases still use 64.

New case control_same_entries_larger_batches admits an observation that can refute the mechanism: a return there, with the hanging case unchanged at 64, attributes the block to batch count rather than entry count.

scope.description: Two leadership-transfer invocations on real four-voter in-memory clusters. In both, a non-leader member is chosen as the explicit target; in the trigger case that member is first demoted to non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API and the committed configuration is allowed to reach it, while the control keeps it a voter. Each case records the transfer future's outcome, whether the named target ever reported Leader, whether the final leader is the target, a sampled leaderless interval and the members' terms after the attempt.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms), so a new election can complete quickly.
The demotion is committed before the transfer is requested; the harness waits 200 ms and does not assert configuration convergence separately.

The leaderless interval is estimated from repeated 10 ms sampling whose measured effective rate was about one sample per 116 ms (43 samples), so a shorter leaderless gap can be missed and a zero count is not evidence of absence.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about the effect on client requests accepted during the transfer window, and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely (rejected earlier by the replState lookup) are not exercised.

basis.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), and selects the first non-leader raft as the target. The trigger calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and sleeps 200 ms; the control skips demotion. The case event records the target role, its term before, and the watch parameters. scope.description: One follower of a three-voter configuration is driven through real AppendEntries RPCs on its transport while a single heartbeat is executed on a separate goroutine, as the fast-path contract permits. A stable store holds the heartbeat's term write until the main thread has persisted the newer term; the run records the persisted term sequence, the node's current term before and after, and the log and FSM contents at the affected indexes after a stale-leader request.
assumptions: The heartbeat is delivered by invoking the registered processHeartbeat handler on a separate goroutine, which is what NetworkTransport's connection handler does; the in-memory transport ignores the registration, so the transport's own dispatch is not exercised.
The stable store delays, but never corrupts or fails, one currentTerm write, modelling a slow store write that completes after a newer term has been persisted.

The term 2 and term 4 AppendEntries requests are supplied by the harness to represent a leader that has committed those indexes elsewhere; their commit indexes are asserted by the request, not produced by a quorum of real nodes.
Election and lease timeouts are raised to 30 s so the follower does not campaign during the sequence.
excluded: No attempt to measure how often the interleaving occurs in a real deployment; the probe only establishes that the interleaving is reachable when a store write is delayed.
No real partition or multi-node cluster is used, and the stale leader's authority is modelled by crafted requests.

basis.prefix: The harness builds an in-memory stable/log store whose SetUint64 blocks one chosen currentTerm value, bootstraps a three-voter configuration containing the local node, and starts NewRaft with 30 s election and lease timeouts so the node stays a follower. It first commits entries 2 and 3 at term 2 through trans.AppendEntries on the real consumer path, then installs the blocking hook for term 3 and starts r.processHeartbeat on a goroutine with a heartbeat carrying term 3. Once the hook reports that the term 3 write is in flight, the harness sends a term 4 AppendEntries with entry 4 and leader commit 4 through the transport, waits for it to apply, then releases the term 3 write. It records the current term before and after the release, the persisted term and the sequence of term writes, and finally sends the stale term 3 leader's AppendEntries carrying conflicting entries 4 and 5 with leader commit 5, recording whether that request was accepted, the log payloads at indexes 4 and 5, the FSM payloads at those indexes, the applied and commit indexes, and whether the applied payload at index 4 differs from the log payload there.
basis.responsibility: Raft requires a server's persisted current term never to decrease and its applied log prefix never to be replaced. The library owns both: it persists the term, it decides when to raise it, and it performs the truncation that can remove an entry. A transport contract that permits concurrent heartbeat delivery does not relax those duties, so the library must make the term update safe against the concurrency it authorises.

comparisons.description: The persisted current term must not fall below a term the node already adopted; a true value contradicts it.
After the regression, the stale leader's conflicting entries must not replace an entry already applied at a higher term; a true value contradicts it.

scope.description: Two hundred attempts per case on a single follower of a three-voter configuration. Each attempt reads the node's current term, starts a fast-path heartbeat carrying that term plus one on its own goroutine, concurrently sends an AppendEntries carrying the term plus two (with one entry and a matching previous-log index) through the real consumer path, waits for both, and counts the attempt as an inversion when the node's term afterwards is below the higher request's term. The first case leaves the stable store undelayed; the second adds a uniform 0-2 ms delay to every current-term write.
assumptions: One node runs; the two peers are addresses only, so each attempt's higher-term request is a supplied leader message rather than a real election outcome.
The heartbeat is delivered by invoking the registered handler on its own goroutine, matching the classification and direct invocation that NetworkTransport performs for this request shape.
The undelayed case is not a control for absence of the defect; it measures how often the race occurs when the store adds no latency of its own.
Attempts run sequentially on the same node and reuse its log; terms advance across attempts and are re-read each time.
excluded: No consequence measurement here: this execution only counts term inversions; the truncation consequence was measured separately in the forced-ordering execution.
No multi-node cluster, no real transport framing and no concurrent client load.

basis.prefix: The harness builds an in-memory stable/log store whose SetUint64 optionally sleeps a uniformly random interval up to a configured maximum before persisting the current term, bootstraps a three-voter configuration containing the local node, and starts NewRaft with 30 s election and lease timeouts so the node stays a follower. For each attempt it reads r.CurrentTerm() and r.LastIndex(), starts r.processHeartbeat on a goroutine with a heartbeat carrying current+1, sends an AppendEntries carrying current+2, the last log index as PrevLogEntry with its stored term, one entry at the next index and leader commit at that index, then waits for both to finish and records whether the current term is below current+2. Each case emits a case event with the attempt count and maximum delay and a result event with the inversion count.
basis.responsibility: Raft requires a server's persisted current term never to decrease. The library owns the term update and it authorises concurrent heartbeat execution through the transport contract, so the update must remain correct under the concurrency it permits regardless of how the store is timed.

comparisons.description: With no added store delay, no attempt may end below the term the main thread persisted.
With 0-2 ms write jitter, no attempt may end below the term the main thread persisted.

scope.description: Two restarts of a follower from a real three-voter in-memory cluster with commit-tracking and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled. The leader commits 8400 commands; the chosen follower accumulates them and its own staged commit index is polled until it exceeds 8200. In the control case that follower additionally takes a snapshot before shutdown; in the trigger case it does not. The cluster is then stopped and only the follower is restarted from its retained stores with a fresh transport, bounded by a five-second observation.
assumptions: All three members run the captured code with inmemConfig timeouts and the in-memory commit-tracking store.
The follower's staged commit index is read from its own log store and is therefore what restoreFromCommittedLogs would consume on restart.
The control's snapshot is taken through the follower's own Snapshot future, so the replay it removes is bounded by that follower's applied state.
NewRaft is invoked on its own goroutine; a case that does not return within five seconds is reported as returned=false rather than failing the harness.
excluded: No leader restart, no snapshot shipped from another node, and no client traffic during the restart.
No claim about the exact snapshot index chosen by the follower's snapshot machinery beyond what the case event records.

basis.prefix: Each case builds a three-voter cluster through makeCluster with CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs, waits for a leader, applies 8400 commands through the leader, and polls the chosen follower's own commit index until it exceeds 8200. In the control it then takes a snapshot on that follower; both cases read the follower's last snapshot index, staged commit index and last log index, shut down the follower and the remaining members, and emit a case event with those values plus the derived replay entries and batches. The harness then calls NewRaft on the follower's retained log, stable and snapshot stores with a fresh transport and a logger-free copy of its config, bounded by five seconds, and emits the returned flag, elapsed time and error.
basis.responsibility: The library owns the size and lifetime of its FSM dispatch channel and the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs on disk before completing NewRaft, so a follower restarting with a legal committed prefix must complete.

comparisons.description: A follower restart whose snapshot bounds the replay must let NewRaft complete.
A follower restart replaying its own committed prefix without a snapshot must let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.

scope.description: Two VerifyLeader invocations on real five-member in-memory clusters. Both bootstrap five voters, demote two non-leader members to non-voters, and disconnect the leader's transport from the two remaining voters in both directions. The trigger leaves the two non-voters reachable; the control also disconnects them. Each case records the reachable member counts, the voter quorum, whether the verification completed and with what error, and the leader state afterwards.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with one-second heartbeat, election and lease timeouts so the leader is not stepped down by the lease check during the short window.
Disconnect removes routing in both directions, modelling a partition that isolates the leader from those members only.
The verification is bounded by a two-second wait; a verification that never completes is reported as completed=false rather than failing the harness.
The demotions are committed through the leader before the partition; the harness does not separately assert each member's view of the new configuration.
excluded: No claim about read serializability beyond what VerifyLeader itself promises; the harness does not issue reads.
No transfer or configuration change during the partition, and no client traffic.

basis.prefix: Each case builds a five-voter in-memory cluster through MakeClusterCustom with one-second heartbeat, election and lease timeouts, waits for a leader, demotes two non-leader members with DemoteVoter, and sleeps 300 ms. It then disconnects the leader's transport from the two remaining voters in both directions and, in the control only, from the two non-voters as well. The case event records member counts and the voter quorum; the harness calls leader.VerifyLeader(), waits up to two seconds for the future, and emits whether it completed, whether it returned nil, its error text and the leader's state afterwards.
basis.responsibility: VerifyLeader is documented as protecting against stale reads after leadership has been lost, so the library owns the definition of the support that satisfies it. The quorum it sizes is a voter quorum, and the messages it counts must therefore be voter acknowledgements; a non-voter cannot contribute to leadership legitimacy.

comparisons.description: Control: with no reachable supporter the verification must not report success.

scope.description: Five restart attempts with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled: a commit-tracking store seeded with 8192 committed command entries (exactly 128 batches at MaxAppendEntries=64), the same seeded store with 8193 entries (129 batches), the same 8193 entries with MaxAppendEntries=1024 (9 batches), and two restarts of retained state produced by a real single-node cluster that committed 8300 commands through the normal leader/commit/apply path, one after an explicit Snapshot() and one without a snapshot. basis.prefix: Per case the harness creates an InmemCommitTrackingStore (and InmemSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, assuranceFSM) and emits startup_case_<case> with the configured MaxAppendEntries, staged commit index, last log index, snapshot index and derived replay batch count. Seeded cases store LogCommand entries 1..N and stage commit index N; control_same_entries_larger_batches seeds the same 8193 entries as trigger_129_batches but builds its Config with MaxAppendEntries=1024. Real-prefix cases call BootstrapCluster for a single voter, start the producing raft with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, wait for leadership, apply 8300 commands through Apply futures on the leader, optionally call Snapshot(), then Shutdown(). The restart then calls NewRaft with a fresh Config (RestoreCommittedLogs=true), a fresh FSM and a fresh transport on the retained stores, bounded by the case timeout; startup_result_<case> records returned, elapsed_ms, error, sampled FSM apply count and the number of newly blocked processLogs/restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutines relative to a pre-case stack sample. The two added cases seed 131072 and 131073 committed command entries and restart with MaxAppendEntries=1024; their case events record the derived batch count and the result events record whether NewRaft returned.
basis.responsibility: The library, not the caller, owns the size and lifetime of its FSM dispatch channel: it chooses the batch size, creates fsmMutateCh, and decides the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs on disk before completing NewRaft, so it must complete for a legal (store, commit index) state rather than block the caller that cannot yet shut it down.

The same 8193 committed entries replayed as 9 batches must let NewRaft complete; a failure here would attribute the block to entry count rather than batch count.
One entry past the 128-batch capacity must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.
A real cluster restart with 130 replay batches must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.

experiments.revision_reason: Adds two cases at MaxAppendEntries=1024 that place the replay exactly at and one entry past the 128-batch capacity derived from the fixed channel size, so the boundary can be checked at an entry count far from the default configuration. semantic_changes: The harness runs two cases: a failed RemoveServer that shrinks the voter set, and a failed AddVoter that grows it.
Event names and the case field are suffixed per case, and two additional comparisons cover the grow-direction control.

scope.description: One two-voter cluster of real nodes over in-memory transports. The leading member's log store fails exactly the write carrying the configuration entry that would remove the other voter. The harness records the configuration index the leader holds afterwards against its last stored log index, then waits for the node to lead again and applies one client command, comparing the resulting commit index with the other voter's last log index. The successor additionally restarts the phantom leader from its own stores after the lone commit and records restart success, whether it regains leadership, whether the commit remains in its log, and whether the peer's log has reached that index. In this revision the restarted node's transport is wired to the surviving peer in both directions before the election window, so the restart outcome reflects the target. The successor runs the scenario twice: a failed RemoveServer that leaves a shrunken phantom configuration containing only the leader, and a failed AddVoter that leaves a grown phantom configuration naming an unreachable member.
assumptions: Both members run the captured code with 300 ms heartbeat, election and lease timeouts and share no state.
The injected failure is a single StoreLogs call returning an error; the store is otherwise the standard in-memory store and accepts later writes.
The harness does not assert which of the two members becomes leader first; it targets whichever one leads when the failure is injected.
A command is treated as committed when its Apply future returns nil, which is the client-visible completion point.
excluded: No restart of the failed node, so the log-derived configuration that would replace the phantom one is not exercised.
No snapshot, no third member and no concurrent client traffic.

basis.prefix: The harness creates two in-memory transports connected to each other, bootstraps the same two-voter configuration on both stores, and starts both rafts with 300 ms timeouts. It waits for a leader, arms that leader's log store to fail the next StoreLogs call, and calls RemoveServer for the other member. It records the returned error, the node's state, the in-memory latest configuration index and servers, and the last stored log index, then waits up to ten seconds for the node to be Leader again, applies one command with a three-second timeout, and emits the commit index, the leader's last log index and the other voter's last log index. The successor then shuts the phantom leader down, creates a fresh in-memory transport on the same address, calls NewRaft with the retained stores and its own config, waits up to ten seconds for Leader state, and emits phantom_restart with restart_ok, restarted_as_leader, leader_last_index, peer_last_index, lone_commit_retained and peer_caught_up. Before starting the restarted node, the harness connects the new transport to the peer's transport and repoints the peer's routing entry for the restarted address, so an election and replication can actually take place. Each case emits its own phantom_case_<case>, phantom_result_<case> and phantom_restart_<case> events; the grow case calls AddVoter('C') instead of RemoveServer.
basis.responsibility: The library owns both the durability of a configuration change and the supporter set used for elections and commitment. A configuration entry that was never stored cannot be the configuration under which the node counts votes or commits entries; reporting the change as failed while adopting it for quorums leaves the caller and the cluster with incompatible views of who must agree.

comparisons.description: The failed configuration write must be reported as a failure in the shrink case.
The in-memory latest configuration must not refer to an index beyond the stored log, even when the failed change would have removed a voter.
A client command committed after the failed removal must be held by a quorum of the committed two-voter configuration; the peer lacking it contradicts this.
Control: the in-memory latest configuration must also not exceed the stored log when the failed change would have added a voter.
Control: a command committed under a grown phantom configuration should still be held by a quorum of the committed configuration, which is what bounds the hazard to the shrinking case.

semantic_changes: The restarted node's fresh transport is connected to the surviving peer and the peer's routing entry is repointed to it, so the restart phase actually exercises recovery.
The restart phase's outcome is therefore attributable to the target rather than to missing transport wiring.

experiments.revision_reason: Generalises the harness to run the same failed-write scenario twice: once removing the other voter (shrink) and once adding an unreachable voter (grow). semantic_changes: The cluster now has three running nodes instead of two, and the added server C is reachable and answers vote and append RPCs rather than being an unreachable name.

The harness partitions the leader from the other committed voter after the failed configuration write, and the control case additionally cuts C, so each case isolates the supporter set the phantom configuration admits.
Two cases replace the earlier shrink/grow pair, and the events report the phantom voter count, C's log index and whether the committed voter holds the committed index.

scope.description: Three real nodes over in-memory transports with 300 ms heartbeat, election and lease timeouts. Nodes A and B are bootstrapped with the committed two-voter configuration {A,B}; node C is started with no configuration and no bootstrap, which is the state of a server named by an AddVoter call before that call is logged, and it is reachable from both committed voters. The leader's log store fails exactly the StoreLogs call carrying AddVoter(C), so the in-memory latest configuration becomes {leader, other committed voter, C} at an index the stored log never reaches. The harness then removes the leader's ability to reach the other committed voter in both directions and records whether the leader re-elects, whether a client command commits, and where each of the three logs ends. The trigger leaves C reachable; the control also removes the leader's ability to reach C.
assumptions: All three nodes run the captured code; C is a genuine raft.Node with an empty log, an empty stable store and no bootstrap configuration, not a stub that merely answers RPCs.
The injected failure is a single StoreLogs call returning an error; the store accepts later writes.
Cutting a route with the in-memory transport's Disconnect models a network partition, not a process stop: the cut node keeps running and keeps its own view.
A command is treated as committed when its Apply future returns nil, the client-visible completion point.
The committed configuration remains {A,B} throughout, so any commit requires both committed voters, and a commit the other committed voter lacks is unsupported by that configuration.
excluded: No restart, no snapshot and no repair of the phantom configuration after the observation.
No non-voter in the committed configuration and no concurrent client traffic.
The partition is applied after the failed configuration write, so a network failure that precedes or coincides with the write is not exercised.

basis.prefix: The harness creates three in-memory transports and connects every pair in both directions, bootstraps the two-voter configuration {A,B} on the stores of A and B, and starts three rafts: A and B from their bootstrapped stores, and C with an empty log, an empty stable store and no configuration, so every membership guard that tests a non-empty server list does not apply to it. It waits up to ten seconds for A or B to lead, records which member leads, arms that leader's log store to fail the next StoreLogs call, and calls AddVoter('C', address-of-C) with a five-second timeout. It emits pg_case_<case> with the returned error, the in-memory latest configuration index and servers, the last stored log index and the number of voters in the phantom configuration. It then disconnects the leader's transport from the other committed voter's address and that voter's transport from the leader's address, and in the control case also disconnects the leader from C and C from the leader. It waits up to ten seconds for the leader to be Leader again, applies one command with a three-second timeout, and emits pg_result_<case> with the re-election flag, the apply result, the leader's commit index, each of the three last log indices, whether the committed voter holds the committed index, whether C holds it, and commit_without_committed_voter, which is true only when the apply succeeded and the other committed voter's log ends below the leader's commit index.
basis.responsibility: The library owns both the durability of a configuration change and the supporter set used for elections and commitment. A configuration entry that was never stored cannot be the configuration under which a node counts votes or commits entries; adopting it anyway lets a server the committed configuration does not include supply the decisive acknowledgement for a commit, so a client is told a command is committed while the committed voters are split.

comparisons.description: The failed configuration write must be reported as a failure in the reachable-new-server case.
The in-memory latest configuration must not refer to an index beyond the stored log after the failed AddVoter.
A command committed while the leader cannot reach the other committed voter must not exist, because the committed two-voter configuration needs that voter.
The other committed voter must hold every committed index, whatever set of acknowledgements the leader counted.
Control: with both the committed voter and the new server cut, the phantom configuration of three voters has no attainable second vote, so the node must not regain leadership.
Control: no command may commit once the only remote voter available to the phantom configuration is also unreachable, which is what shows the trigger's commit depended on that server.

semantic_changes: The result event now repeats the reported failure flag add_failed, which the earlier revision emitted only on the case event; no other event field was added or removed.
The cluster, the injected failure, the partitions, the event names and all six comparisons are unchanged, so the receipt is directly comparable with the first one for this experiment.
